payload.claim: The Notes section states "Criterion 2's wrong version failed its witness and six of the parametrized cases," but building that wrong version literally (a mutation of `context_enumeration` returning every backticked token up to the entry's blank line, with no raise) and running it against the full suite including the new test built from criterion 1's spelled-out witness shows 8 failures, not 7: the stated six parametrized cases, criterion 2's own witness, and also criterion 1's new witness (`test_the_reader_refuses_each_definition_the_renderer_refuses`), whose first entry is a single unterminated paragraph with no blank line, causing its first `pytest.raises(ValueError)` to fail since this mutant never raises. This overlap looks unavoidable for any faithful build of the described wrong version, since both tests call the one mutated `context_enumeration`, and it has no consequence for the review process since criterion 2's own named witness still fails as required, but the count in the prose is off by one.
